text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Wednesday it is offering one-day reverse repos at 16.0 percent and one-day repos at 18.0 percent.
He said this effectively cuts the overnight borrowing rate to 16.0 percent from 18.0 percent, and overnight lending rate to 18.0 percent from 20.0 percent starting Thursday.
"We'll cut the rates starting tomorrow. The Monetary Board just approved it," Singson told reporters after meeting with the Monetary Board members.

He said the move was agreed after the peso-dollar market stabilised in recent days. The Central Bank was forced to hike its benchmark rates two weeks ago to quell speculation against the peso at the height of the Thai baht crisis.
"The PDS (Philippine Dealing System) is very quiet at of this time. We are neither buyer nor seller in the market," he said.
The peso is wedged in a tight range of 26.373 and 26.374 to the U.S. dollar.
The Monetary Board is the highest policy making body of the Central Bank. Singson is the chairman of the board.
